Synchronize documents

Source: R/doc.R
doc_sync.Rd

Replicas exchange state as raw vectors, which can be written to disk or sent over any transport.

  • doc_export() serializes a whole document as a snapshot: its contents and full history.

  • doc_export_updates() serializes only the changes made since the version from, or the complete history when from is NULL. from may also be a document, which stands for its current version: the export then holds exactly the changes that document is missing.

  • doc_export_shallow() serializes a shallow snapshot: the contents plus only the history after the version since. Dropping old history can make the export much smaller for a document with a long history, but a document loaded from it cannot check out versions before since or merge edits that branch off before it.

  • doc_import() merges a snapshot or updates into a document. Importing is commutative and idempotent, so replicas that have seen the same updates hold the same contents. bytes may also be a list of raw vectors, which are imported together in one step.

  • doc_merge() imports into doc every change from the document source that doc does not have yet. It is short for doc_import(doc, doc_export_updates(source, from = doc)), for replicas in the same R session; replicas in different processes exchange the raw vectors instead.

  • doc_version() returns the document's current version vector, for use as the from argument of doc_export_updates(). See as_version().

  • doc_is_shallow() reports whether a document lacks its early history because it was loaded from a shallow snapshot.

  • blob_metadata() describes an exported raw vector without importing it.

  • doc_export_json() and doc_import_json() exchange changes as JSON text. This is larger than the binary format but readable, and useful for inspection and debugging. JSON cannot carry values nested more than about 120 levels deep: such a document exports, but the result cannot be imported again. It also cannot carry containers created with map_ensure_container(), and doc_export_json() refuses to export changes that create one.

Usage

doc_export(doc)

doc_export_updates(doc, from = NULL)

doc_export_shallow(doc, since = NULL)

doc_import(doc, bytes)

doc_merge(doc, source)

doc_import_status(doc)

doc_version(doc)

doc_is_shallow(doc)

blob_metadata(bytes)

doc_export_json(doc, from = NULL, to = NULL)

doc_import_json(doc, json)

Arguments

doc

A loro_doc.

from

A version returned by doc_version() to start from, typically that of the replica the updates are destined for, or NULL for the beginning. doc_export_updates() also accepts a loro_doc, standing for its current version.

since

A version: frontiers from doc_frontiers(), or the version after one change, named by its number in doc_changes() order or by its commit message. The default, the latest version, keeps no earlier history at all.

bytes

A raw vector produced by one of the export functions, or for doc_import() a list of them.

source

The loro_doc to merge changes from.

to

A version returned by doc_version() to stop at, or NULL for the latest.

json

A string produced by doc_export_json().

Value

doc_export(), doc_export_updates(), and doc_export_shallow() return a raw vector and doc_version() a version vector. doc_import(), doc_merge(), and doc_import_json() return doc invisibly, and doc_import_status() returns an import status or NULL; see the Import status section. doc_is_shallow() returns a logical, doc_export_json() a string, and blob_metadata() a list with mode, changes (the number of changes), start_timestamp and end_timestamp, and the versions start_frontiers, start_version, and end_version.

Import status

doc_import(), doc_merge(), and doc_import_json() return the document invisibly, so they can be used in a pipe. The outcome of the most recent import into a document is kept with it, and doc_import_status() returns it, or NULL if nothing has been imported. Like the document, it is shared by every reference to it, so it can be read from the original variable as well as from the result of a pipe. It is a list of two tibbles, success and pending, each with columns peer, start, and end giving a range of that peer's operation counters. success holds the operations that were applied. pending holds operations that arrived before the changes they depend on; they are kept and applied automatically once the missing changes are imported. A non-empty pending means an earlier update was lost or is still in transit.

Examples

a = loro_doc()
text_insert(a, 1, "Hello")

b = loro_doc()
doc_import(b, doc_export(a))

text_insert(a, 6, " world")
text_insert(b, 1, ">> ")

# Send `b` the changes it is missing, as raw bytes
bytes = doc_export_updates(a, from = doc_version(b))
doc_import(b, bytes)
doc_import_status(b)
#> $success
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   peer                start   end
#>   <chr>               <int> <int>
#> 1 9933661713059498580     5    11
#> 
#> $pending
#> # A tibble: 0 × 3
#> # ℹ 3 variables: peer <chr>, start <int>, end <int>
#> 

# In one R session, merge directly
doc_merge(a, b) |>
  text_get()
#> [1] ">> Hello world"
text_get(b)
#> [1] ">> Hello world"

# Imports return the document, so they can be piped
loro_doc() |> doc_import(doc_export(a)) |> text_get()
#> [1] ">> Hello world"

small = doc_export_shallow(a)
blob_metadata(small)$mode
#> [1] "shallow-snapshot"
